messages:
sre-oncall: :rotating_light: Incident opened - CUDA OOMs observed on serving nodes despite reported headroom. Root ts: 1950005678

sre-oncall: Symptoms: sudden spike in CUDA OOM errors in runtime logs, nodes reporting >90% reserved blocks used, fragmentation ratio up from 0.12 -> 0.48 in last 20m. Some containers killed (OOM) causing request 5xxs.

infra-monitor: automated alert: 6 nodes flagged (g5/rt), 03:12 UTC, error sample attached: ```[2026-03-15T03:12:21Z] cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory ... reserved_blocks=512MB headroom=768MB free=200MB fragmentation=0.46``` 

carlos: I'm on it. Any recent deploys? Check last deploy 03:05? dev-bot shows no runtime release, but kernel bump earlier today.

dev-bot: Deploy check: last infra change: kernel/driver update deployed to g5 pool at 02:58 UTC by infra-deploy.

anya: Could be KV cache reservation semantics + fragmentation. If allocator uses slabed reservations, fragmentation can make headroom misleading.

maria: Manual mitigation suggestions: 1) Drain most affected nodes 2) Evict large KV caches (runtime API) 3) Reduce per-request KV reservation (if allowed) 4) Roll traffic to fallback model variant.

support-ops: Customer impact: At least 3 tenants reporting increased 500s; one Enterprise customer (AcmeInc) seeing ~17% error rate on embeddings requests. Notified them and creating status update.

sre-oncall: Executing drain on node g5-node-12: ```kubectl cordon g5-node-12 && kubectl drain g5-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force``` 

infra-bot: Node cordoned/drain started on g5-node-12. Eviction of pods in progress.

carlos: Evicted large models on that node, but JVM runtimes keep holding reserved blocks. Sending command to runtime to evict KV cache: ```curl -X POST http://runtime/g5-node-12/admin/evict_kv_cache -d '{"percent":100}'``` 

anya: Querying metrics: ```promql: avg by(node) (cuda_memory_free_bytes / cuda_memory_total_bytes)```. Nodes g5-node-11/12/13 show free fraction ~0.18 vs expected ~0.4. Fragmentation metric: `cuda_memory_fragmentation_ratio` trending up.

maria: Quick config tweak: lowering HEADROOM_RESERVE_MB from 1024 -> 512 on affected pool via config service. Will patch canary nodes first.

dev-bot: Patching runtime config on pool serving-highmem-canary: ```/api/configs/patch pool=serving-highmem-canary HEADROOM_RESERVE_MB=512``` -> queued

sre-oncall: Also disabling KV-prefix caching for a minute to see effect: ```kubectl -n infra set env deploy/runtime KV_PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false``` 

carlos: After evictions and config change, OOM rate decreased on g5-node-12. Logs show allocator returning more contiguous free ranges. Looks promising.

support-ops: Sending status update to AcmeInc: "We've identified memory fragmentation + reserved-block mismatch as cause; mitigation in progress; expect partial improvement within 15-30m." 

maria: We still see a second wave on g5-node-11. Starting rolling restarts of runtime-agent on affected nodes to clear allocator state: ```systemctl restart runtime-agent``` (or restart container)

infra-bot: Restart orchestration: 3 nodes restarted, 2 still restarting.

anya: Note: this is likely a specific path where small allocations cause many reserved blocks to be pinned (KV cache + prefix caching). Recommend long-term: change allocation strategy to prefer coalescing and reduce slab sizes.

carlos: Filing runtime issue: #RT-1453 "reserved-block pinning under high KV churn causes fragmentation despite headroom" with logs and heapshots.

maria: Customer impact update: AcmeInc error rate down to 4% after mitigations. Other tenants trending to normal. Marking Incident as partial mitigated.

sre-oncall: Handoff to night team @anya. Leaving runbook notes: actions taken, nodes drained, config changes, runtime issue filed. Please monitor `cuda_error_count` and `model_serving_5xx_rate` and escalate if >5% for 10m.

anya: Acknowledged. I'll follow up with a postmortem draft tomorrow. TY everyone :heart:

support-ops: I'll close customer loop once we have a full postmortem. :+1:
